solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Individual outside school expected to collect learner as planned

indicators.note: the word for an individual is placed around the school abbreviation

parts.note: a single individual is one

indicators.note: the word for expected gathers the learner letter into its middle

parts.note: something expected is due
L is a learner, from the L-plate on a learner driver's car

explanation.surface: A lone person outside a school, due to pick up a pupil, arrives as arranged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' wraps the first pair of pieces and 'to collect' wraps the second; 'expected' is not part of the definition but the word due.
explanation.definitionFit: Something happening on time, at the arranged hour, is happening as it was planned.

clue.text: Thick smoke ascending to obscure this Russian city

indicators.note: ascending says the hidden letters are read backwards
the words thick smoke cover up the city's letters, which lie concealed across them

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Thick smoke rising to blot out a Russian city.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'obscure' into the definition, but 'to obscure' is the signal that the letters KSMO lie inside 'Thick smoke'; 'ascending', in a down clue, reads them upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Omsk is a large city in south-western Siberia, so it is a Russian city.

clue.text: Bird — one to push across 'orrible place

indicators.note: the word for a pusher stretches across the dropped-aitch place, holding it

parts.note: a shover is someone who pushes
hell with its H dropped, as in a Cockney 'orrible, gives 'ell

explanation.surface: A bird described as one that pushes its way into a horrible spot.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in ''orrible' tells you to drop the H from HELL too, giving ELL.
explanation.definitionFit: The shoveler (also spelt shoveller) is a dabbling duck with a broad, spoon-like bill.

clue.text: Poor king being deposed and brought to trial

indicators.note: a deposed king is removed from his place, so the king letter is taken out

parts.note: someone poor is hard up
R stands for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A poor king, overthrown, is put on trial.
explanation.definitionFit: To be had up is a British idiom for being summoned before a court to face a charge.

clue.text: Aggressive expert — this writer with article penned

indicators.note: penned means shut in, as in a pen, so the skilful word encloses the other pieces

parts.note: an expert, skilful hand is deft
the writer of the clue refers to themself as I
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A combative expert: the writer, with an article he has penned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'penned' looks like writing an article, but it means enclosed.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone defiant is openly resisting and confrontational, which is an aggressive stance.

clue.text: Moody maybe in lead, wrecking play

indicators.note: the actor's first name sits inside the rearranged letters
wrecking the word lead breaks its letters up and reassembles them

parts.note: taken as written
Ron Moody was the actor who played Fagin in the film Oliver!

explanation.surface: An actor, perhaps Moody, in the lead role, ruining the play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moody' looks like a mood, but is the actor who played Fagin in Oliver!; 'wrecking' scrambles lead, and 'in' sets the actor's name inside.
explanation.definitionFit: La Ronde is Arthur Schnitzler's play, a chain of ten linked seductions.

clue.text: Brief description plausible but wrong, not half

indicators.note: only half of the word is kept, here its first four letters

parts.note: a specious argument seems plausible but is in fact false

explanation.surface: A short account that sounds right but is wrong, not even half true.
explanation.definitionFit: A spec, short for specification, is a concise description of what is required.

clue.text: I should be evident in model

definitions.text: I should be evident in model

indicators.note: the letter I appears within the modelling word

parts.note: a model poses, so to pose is to model

explanation.surface: A model, speaking, says self-possession should show in her.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: I inside POSE, and composure is what a model should show.
explanation.definitionFit: Graceful composure and balance is exactly the quality a fashion model is expected to display.

clue.text: Musical man? One who has got the sack, we hear!

indicators.note: says the words are judged by how they sound when spoken

parts.words: One who has got the sack
parts.note: a coal porter carries coal in a sack on his back

explanation.surface: A musician who, it seems, has been fired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'got the sack' suggests dismissal, but means literally carrying one. Cole Porter was the American songwriter of Kiss Me, Kate.
explanation.definitionFit: Cole Porter wrote musicals such as Anything Goes, so he is a man of musicals.

clue.text: Start of solemn declaration bringing war

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the following word is used

parts.note: a word is a declaration or promise, as in giving one's word

explanation.surface: A formal declaration begins, and war follows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bringing' is a link; the sword stands for war itself, as in 'the pen is mightier than the sword'.
explanation.definitionFit: By metonymy the weapon of battle stands for military force and warfare.

clue.text: Female about to go to doctor, unwell — one admitted for emergency procedure

indicators.note: the numeral is let in between the female and about letters

parts.note: re means about or concerning
I is the Roman numeral one
unwell means ill

explanation.surface: A woman about to see the doctor, sick, is admitted for emergency treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'admitted' sounds like a hospital admission but puts I inside FRE.
explanation.definitionFit: A practice evacuation in case of fire is a drill rehearsing what to do in an emergency.

clue.text: Detective being created by author

parts.note: a dick is slang for a detective, especially a private eye
ens is a philosophical term for being or existence

explanation.surface: A detective character dreamed up by a writer.
explanation.walkthrough: ENS, Latin for 'being', is a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Dickens was the Victorian novelist who wrote Oliver Twist and Bleak House.

clue.text: Account for reason why man with roving eye sought new lover?

definitions.meaning: to account for something is to give reasons for it

definitions.text: reason why man with roving eye sought new lover?
definitions.meaning: his former partner was unattractive: the ex was plain

explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as EX PLAIN: the cryptic second reading is a whimsical excuse for straying.
explanation.definitionFit: To account for something is to make it clear by giving the reasons, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Indian page who tries to suck up to boss?

definitions.text: who tries to suck up to boss?

parts.note: the Cree are a Native American people of Canada

explanation.surface: An Indian page boy who is trying to flatter his master.
explanation.definitionFit: A sycophant who fawns on superiors is a creep, an informal term of contempt.

clue.text: Careful performance's ending with funny entertaining number

indicators.note: ending says only the final letter of the word performance is used
the funny word takes in, as a host entertains a guest, the number abbreviation

parts.note: something funny is comical

explanation.surface: A careful show that ends with a comic routine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entertaining' looks like an adjective for the show but means holding something inside; 'ending' picks the last letter of performance.
explanation.definitionFit: Being sparing and thrifty with resources means being careful with money.

clue.text: Channel offering cruel TV broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast also means scattered, so the letters are spread and resown in a new order

explanation.surface: A television channel that puts out harsh programmes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Channel' looks like a TV channel, but is a drain.
explanation.definitionFit: A culvert is a tunnel or drain carrying water under a road, a kind of channel.

clue.text: Survive after revolution and note uprising as historically significant

indicators.note: a revolution turns the word right round, so it is read backwards

parts.note: to cope is to manage or survive

indicators.note: in a down clue an uprising reads the note from the bottom upwards

parts.note: lah is the sixth note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Surviving a revolution and a rising, both events of historic weight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after revolution' and 'uprising' both turn their words backwards; 'and' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Something marking a new era or age is momentous, hence historically significant.

clue.text: Horse is calmer, having bitten trainer initially

indicators.note: the calmer word has its teeth around the trainer's first letter

parts.note: more even in temper, so evener

indicators.note: only the first letter of the word trainer is used

explanation.surface: A horse that settles down after biting its trainer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' is a link; EVENER with T inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse trained for eventing, the three-part equestrian competition, is called an eventer.

clue.text: Boys initially introduced to Latin are working as learners should be

indicators.note: the letter is brought in among the rearranged letters
the words Latin are are put to work in a new order
only the first letter of the word boys is used

explanation.surface: Boys starting Latin are hard at work, just as pupils should be.
explanation.walkthrough: LATIN ARE rearranged gives TRAINALE, with B slipped in.
explanation.definitionFit: Learners ought to be capable of being taught, which is what trainable means.

clue.text: Overseas we will be full of hesitation, very timid

indicators.note: the French word is filled with the other letters

parts.note: nous is French for we, a foreign word from across the sea
er is the sound of someone hesitating

explanation.surface: Abroad we are full of hesitation and very shy.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone nervous is easily frightened and anxious, a close synonym for timid.

clue.text: Audible search for drink and food by the coast

indicators.note: says the words are judged by how they sound when spoken

parts.note: to search is to seek, and ale is a drink

explanation.surface: A noisy hunt for a drink and something to eat at the seaside.
explanation.definitionFit: Sea kale is an edible plant that grows wild on shingle beaches, so it is coastal food.

clue.text: Someone with secure accommodation having floor at back of house

indicators.note: the floor word goes behind the house abbreviation

parts.note: a stage is a floor or level of a building

explanation.surface: Someone with a safe home that has an extra floor at the back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'secure accommodation' sounds like a desirable home but means being held captive.
explanation.definitionFit: A captive held to force a deal is kept under lock and key, in secure confinement.

clue.text: Job description for beer-maker (male) in book

parts.note: the male pronoun
what a maker of beer does is to brew, said of him in the third person

explanation.surface: A job description for a man who brews beer, printed in a book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Job' hints at the biblical book of Job, but the answer is another book of the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: The Epistle to the Hebrews is a book of the New Testament.

clue.text: Name of little women in demonstration

definitions.meaning: the four sisters in Louisa May Alcott's novel Little Women share this surname
a protest walk or parade by demonstrators

explanation.definitionFit: The Little Women sisters Meg, Jo, Beth and Amy are the Marches; a protest procession is also a march.

clue.text: Remote-controlled vehicle finished under river

indicators.note: in a down clue the finished word sits below the river letter

parts.note: something finished is over

explanation.surface: A remote-control vehicle ends up beneath a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A planetary rover, like those on Mars, is a vehicle driven by remote control.

clue.text: White book unit in print shop

parts.note: an album is a book for photos or stamps
an en is a printer's unit of measurement, half an em

explanation.surface: A white-paged book set up in the printer's workshop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'White' looks like paper colour but means egg white.
explanation.definitionFit: Albumen is the white of an egg, the clear part that whitens when cooked.

clue.text: Stars appearing down under, a bright bunch

definitions.meaning: a faint constellation, the Table Mountain, seen only from the southern hemisphere
the society whose members have high IQs

explanation.definitionFit: Mensa is both a southern constellation and the society for people of high intelligence.

clue.text: What litres poured into stomach may constitute!

definitions.text: What litres poured into stomach may constitute!

indicators.note: the litres letter flows inside the stomach word

parts.note: the gut is the stomach or belly

explanation.surface: Pouring many litres into your belly could amount to an excess.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: L inside GUT, and too much liquid in the stomach is an oversupply.
explanation.definitionFit: An excessive quantity, more than can be taken in, is a surfeit or oversupply.

clue.text: A bounder grabbing girl (or boy) in church procession

indicators.note: the pieces all go within the church letters

parts.note: CE stands for the Church of England
Val is a name for either sex, short for Valerie or Valentine
a cad is a bounder, an ungentlemanly man, here seizing the girl

explanation.surface: A rogue grabbing a girl, or maybe a boy, during a church parade.
explanation.walkthrough: Val can be a man's or a woman's name, hence the bracket.
explanation.definitionFit: A cavalcade is a formal procession, originally one on horseback.

clue.text: Christmas book included famous Swede

indicators.note: the book letter is taken inside the Christmas word

parts.note: Noel is another word for Christmas

explanation.surface: A Christmas book featuring a celebrated Swede.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfred Nobel, inventor of dynamite and founder of the prizes, was a Swedish chemist.

clue.text: Stories from either extreme of literature

wordplay.reading: the letter L or the letter E

parts.note: the word literature begins with L and ends with E

explanation.surface: Tales drawn from the far ends of literature.
explanation.definitionFit: Lore is a body of traditional tales and knowledge handed down, so stories.

clue.text: I feel tact's inappropriate — we must be honest

indicators.note: inappropriate says the letters are out of their proper place and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone decides tact is out of place and it is time for candour.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom introduces an unwelcome truth, admitting frankly what has to be said.
